title: Frontend: Throttle
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Throttle. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Implement solution({wait,calls,end}). Deterministically model a leading+trailing throttle. calls are [time,value] in nondecreasing integer milliseconds; timers at a timestamp fire before calls there. Return [executionTime,value] events through inclusive end. A solitary leading call has no trailing duplicate. wait > 0.
constraints: Define solution(input) in plain JavaScript. Return the documented JSON-compatible value or throw the documented validation error. Each case receives a fresh input.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Track the last invocation time, pending timer, and latest receiver/arguments.
alternativeApproaches: Add flush and define whether it changes the next allowed invocation deadline.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Single call; burst; boundary time.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
